brief.ask: Art-direct "Stained Glass Rose Caustics" — #6 of the 72 Ambo church visualizers (Calm Contemporary Worship lyric visualizer, Collection I of 72; subgenre Sacred Architecture). Premise: Twelve-petal Gothic rose window with quatrefoil cusps and jewel caustics. A twelve-petal Gothic cathedral rose window with pointed lancets, quatrefoil medallions, and leaded stone tracery casts jewel-toned caustics. Lighting today: Key: Sunlight filtered through antique ruby, cobalt, emerald, and gold glass. Service use: Liturgical worship, Doxology, Trinity Sunday, sacred choral pieces. Audio mapping today: Harmonic → Blends ruby, sapphire, emerald, and gold caustic petals; Swell → Expands the radial rose aperture and caustic throw; Vocal → Brightens leaded glass rim highlights & central rosette. Palette: #0A0B14 #1E3A7A #A8243B #E8A838. Keep the id, name, premise and palette; rebuild the direction: the geometry and depth planes, typography for the worship lyric band (one line at a time, four to five seconds a line, word-by-word progression), image logic (how the procedural scene (no concept plate: the plate is generative, in code) and the procedural scene meet), texture, motion, and which audio channel drives what. Decide it — the lead's lens will drive the kit's material weave and optical pass for this one.
brief.audience: Congregations watching a projector or LED wall from the pews, five to forty metres away, eyes on the words; and the worship leader or volunteer running Ambo live from a laptop.
brief.feeling: Stillness and reverence — a sanctuary that breathes with the singer's voice; gorgeous, slow, never a screensaver.
constraints: Build method (fixed): a real-time Canvas 2D audio-reactive renderer in Plajah's worship visualizer kit — sanctuary background, multi-plane depth (god rays, motes, bokeh), the kit's Council optical pass (35mm light leaks, anamorphic flare, film grain, colour punch, and a tactile material weave keyed to the LEAD director's lens) and the kit's lyric / scripture typography engine. No video playback, no WebGL, no assets beyond the one concept plate.

Audio drives amplitude, colour, light, growth and glow only — never the position of the words. Envelopes are smoothed; nothing strobes or flashes (photosensitive-safe); uptempo pulses are spring-damped.

The reading band is sacred: lyrics or scripture must stay legible at 1920×1080 and 4K from the back pew, over the busiest moment of the scene. A text-safe dimming band is part of the kit; direct how the scene yields to it.

Typefaces are fixed to the kit's open-licensed set: Noto Serif (text serif), Outfit / Inter (sans), Cinzel (display), JetBrains Mono. Direct scale, case, tracking, measure and hierarchy, not new families.

Sacred imagery is used correctly and respectfully: biblical places and objects are specific and attributable, never costume; nothing denominational or branded; nothing that reads as a music video or a screensaver.
Runs at 60 fps on an integrated-GPU laptop driving a projector: favour layered gradients, cached textures and a few large shapes over particle storms.
Keep this visualizer's id, name, premise and four-colour palette. The council owns the direction, not the catalogue entry.
references: No concept plate: the scene is built entirely in code from the premise.
Sample lyric lines on the band: "Be still my soul the Lord is on thy side" / "Bear patiently the cross of grief or pain".

proposals.title: Light Governed by Stone
proposals.idea: The rose window is not a decoration behind the words — it is the cantus firmus: a single polar-coordinate light source declared before any content exists, from which every caustic petal, leaded tracery line, shadow offset, and lyric entrance interval is derived as a consequent voice.
proposals.geometry: A 12-fold polar grid (30° sectors, each subdivided by the golden ratio φ = 1.618 into inner medallion radius r₁ and outer lancet tip r₂) is the sole structural authority. The canvas is divided into three depth planes: Plane 0 — deep field, a radial gradient from #0A0B14 at centre expanding to near-black at edge, carrying the stone oculus silhouette as a cached arc; Plane 1 — the window itself, 12 petal trapezoids and 12 quatrefoil medallion outlines drawn in procedural Canvas 2D arcs, leaded lines 2 px at rest; Plane 2 — the caustic throw, 12 elliptical light pools projected forward onto the nave floor plane at a 15° declination, each keyed to its petal colour (ruby A8243B, cobalt 1E3A7A, emerald derived, gold E8A838 in strict 4-3-3-2 petal rotation). The lyric band occupies a text-safe horizontal zone at 62% of canvas height — below the window's equator, above the caustic floor — 18% ca
proposals.typography: Cinzel for the lyric band: all-caps small-capitals, tracked at +0.12 em, centred, set at 5.2 vw (scales to ~56 px at 1080p, ~112 px at 4K). Line measure held to 68 characters maximum so no line wraps. Word-by-word reveal: each word fades in over 180 ms, sits full opacity for its syllabic duration (minimum 320 ms per word), then the completed line holds until the next line is cued — no wipe, no slide, only opacity. The outgoing line dissolves over 600 ms as the incoming line's first word appears; the two never overlap at full opacity. Noto Serif italic at 1.6 vw for scripture attribution below the lyric line, tracking +0.06 em, luminance held at 55% of lyric luminance. No sans-serif in the sacred register; Outfit/Inter reserved for the operator's HUD overlay only, never projected.
proposals.imageLogic: No imported image assets. The scene is entirely procedural: the concept plate is the code itself. The rose window is rendered each frame as layered Canvas 2D arcs — outer pointed lancets drawn with bezierCurveTo following the φ-grid radii, quatrefoil cusps as four-arc clusters at r₁, leaded lines as 2 px strokes in #0A0B14 at 80% opacity. Caustic pools are radial gradients (jewel colour → transparent) drawn on Plane 2 with globalCompositeOperation 'lighter', ellipse-transformed by ctx.setTransform to simulate floor-plane projection. God rays are eight thin conic gradients at 22.5° offsets from the key light azimuth, opacity 0.06 at rest. Film grain is a per-frame noise pass: a 4×4 px dithered luminance jitter at ±3% applied via a small offscreen canvas tiled across the full surface — large shape, cheap cost. Anamorphic flare: a single horizontal gaussian streak through the window centre,
proposals.texture: Stone tracery is simulated by a cached 1920×1080 offscreen canvas drawn once at load: the oculus rim, the mullion ribs between lancets, and the outer moulding ring, all rendered as filled arcs in a mid-dark desaturated blue-grey (#1A1E2A) with a 1 px inner highlight stroke at 30% white opacity to suggest carved edge relief. This cache never redraws unless canvas resizes. The leaded glass interiors receive a subtle radial vignette per petal (centre 12% lighter than edge) to simulate glass thickness variation. The material weave for the Classical optical pass is parchment-grain: the noise pass uses a slow-scrolling (0.4 px/s vertical) Perlin-approximated luminance field at 8% opacity over the entire canvas, giving the projected image the faint tooth of aged vellum rather than the flatness of a screen — this is the tactile register that identifies the Classical lens in the kit.
proposals.motion: All motion is governed by three audio envelopes — Harmonic, Swell, Vocal — each low-pass filtered at τ = 0.18 s to prevent strobing. Temporal hierarchy is fixed: the stone plane (Plane 0) never moves. Plane 1 (window) breathes at Swell: the outer lancet tips translate radially by ±1.2% of canvas radius (spring k=0.06, damping 0.82), so the window appears to expand and contract like a slow breath — never more than perceptible from the back pew, never less than felt. Plane 2 (caustic pools): Harmonic drives per-petal opacity — ruby and cobalt petals respond to lower harmonic bins, emerald and gold to upper, so a chord blend shifts the colour balance of the floor light without any petal ever disappearing entirely (floor opacity range 0.18–0.72). God rays: Swell amplitude lifts god-ray opacity from 0.06 to 0.18 over 1.4 s, returns over 2.1 s. Anamorphic flare: Vocal amplitude above 0.6 trigg
proposals.productionMethod: Real-time Canvas 2D renderer, 60 fps target on integrated GPU. All geometry is procedural: φ-grid constants exported as code constants before the render loop initialises — these are the cantus firmus, never renegotiated at runtime. Offscreen canvas for stone tracery cache (drawn once). Offscreen canvas for 64×64 Perlin-approximated noise tile (redrawn every 3 frames, scrolled by transform). Main render loop: clear → draw Plane 0 gradient → blit stone cache → draw Plane 1 window petals (arcs, no images) → draw Plane 2 caustic pools (lighter composite) → draw god rays → apply dimming band → draw lyric type → apply grain tile (screen composite, low opacity) → draw flare streak. Audio Web Audio API AnalyserNode, FFT 1024, three frequency-band RMS extractors (bass/mid/high mapped to Harmonic/Swell/Vocal), all outputs passed through exponential smoothing before any draw call reads them.
proposals.humanTrace: The parchment-grain noise field scrolls at a pace that reads as breath, not computation. The 2 px leaded lines carry a hand-pressure analogue: their highlight brightens under Vocal as a calligrapher's edge catches a candle. The φ-grid proportions are not algorithmic convenience — they are the same ratio Villard de Honnecourt used to set the nave elevation of Gothic cathedrals, cited here as structural method, not ornament. The word-by-word lyric reveal is paced to spoken-word cadence, not to BPM, because the text is the primary sacred object and must be read, not watched.
proposals.risk: The strict cantus-firmus discipline — φ-grid declared first, every element derived from it, nothing permitted outside the system — risks producing a scene that feels hermetic to a congregation expecting warmth. A rose window built entirely from arcs and gradients, with no painterly accident, could read as diagrammatic rather than devotional. The risk is worth carrying because the alternative — arbitrary caustic positions, decorative motion unmoored from structure — would produce exactly the screensaver effect the brief forbids. If the proportions are right, the system disappears and what remains is light that seems to know where it is going.

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist will want the caustic reveal to announce itself — a sudden bloom, a swell that crests and breaks visibly, a moment the congregation recognises as climax. I refuse this on structural grounds: in a Gothic nave, the light does not perform its arrival. It is already there when you enter; your eye discovers it. proposals.title: Lead Traced, Glass Bleeds Light
proposals.idea: The rose window is not a backdrop — it is a registration plate: twelve lead-line vectors are committed in code before any caustic renders, and every halo, petal bloom, and lyric glow must answer to those prior marks the way ink must answer to the press.
proposals.geometry: Twelve-fold radial armature declared as a single pre-render constant array: twelve unit vectors at 30° increments, each carrying a petal width, a lancet aperture angle, and a quatrefoil cusp radius — these are the registration marks the whole scene is accountable to. Three depth planes: rear plane holds the leaded stone window as a dark tracery mesh drawn with Canvas 2D arc-and-bezier strokes, 2–4 px line weight, opacity 0.55, fixed; mid plane holds the caustic throw — twelve colored ellipse-fans (ruby, cobalt, emerald, gold cycling to palette) whose radii and opacity answer to Harmonic amplitude, origin always locked to the declared petal vectors; near plane holds god-ray shafts (four large conic gradients, fixed azimuth 35°) and slow-drifting motes (eight circles, radius 3–7 px, no more). Central rosette: single circle, r = 9% of short edge, filled with a radial gradient from #E8A838 c
proposals.typography: Cinzel, display weight, all-caps, tracked +0.14em, set at 4.2vw for the primary lyric line — this is a cathedral inscription, not a subtitle. Single line at a time. Word-by-word reveal: each word fades in at 180ms ease-out, no slide, no bounce — appearance only, because the words do not move. Line hold: 4–5 seconds. Line exit: full line fades to 0 at 320ms ease-in before next line enters. Below the lyric, a rule — 1 px, #E8A838, 38% opacity, 24 vw wide, centered — then a scripture or title tag in Noto Serif italic, 1.6vw, tracking +0.06em, #E8A838 at 70% opacity. No drop shadow. Instead: a soft outer glow on the Cinzel letterforms, blur-radius 18 px, color #1E3A7A at 60% opacity, drawn as a Canvas shadowBlur pass before the fill — the letters appear to be lit from inside the glass, not spotlit from above. All text color: #FFFFFF at 96% opacity over the dimming band. Minimum tap target ir
proposals.imageLogic: No concept plate, no photograph, no scan. The window is entirely procedural: Canvas 2D draws the tracery mesh from the pre-declared 12-vector array each frame (paths cached to an offscreen canvas, redrawn only on resize). Caustics are elliptical gradient fills — each petal gets one ellipse whose major axis aligns to its registered vector, color cycling ruby → cobalt → emerald → gold → ruby around the 12 positions. The glass color itself bleeds: at the petal boundary, a second smaller ellipse in the adjacent petal color overlaps at 25% opacity, simulating the actual physics of light mixing through leaded glass. The 35° god-ray shafts are four conic gradients anchored at top-left at that fixed angle — same angle declared once, used by every specular calculation in the pass. Nothing enters from outside the code.
proposals.texture: The kit's material weave for this lens is simulated lead and antique glass: film grain at 18% opacity, monochrome, large-grain (noise scale 3–5 px) — not fine digital noise but the grain of a slow film stock pushed in low light. Over the caustic layer only: a multiply-blended vignette that darkens the caustic edges by 40%, simulating the way antique glass holds light in its center and dies at the lead line. The optical pass adds: 35mm light leak as a warm horizontal smear (#E8A838, 8% opacity, fixed position upper-right, never animated by audio — it is a physical fact of the frame, not a reaction). Anamorphic flare: one horizontal streak from the central rosette, 1 px tall, 60% of frame width, color #E8A838 at 12% opacity, drawn only when Vocal amplitude exceeds 0.6 — a single material event, not a loop. Colour punch: global Canvas filter set to saturate(1.15) contrast(1.08), applied onc
proposals.motion: Everything moves at the speed of breath and slower. Caustic petals: Harmonic amplitude drives a spring-damped scale factor (spring k=0.04, damping 0.82) on each petal ellipse's radii — at rest, petals sit at 70% of max size; at full Harmonic, they reach 100%. They never exceed their registered vector bounds. Swell channel: drives a slow radial expansion of the entire mid-plane caustic group — a single scalar applied to all petal ellipse positions, moving them outward from center by up to 8% of frame width. Envelope smoothed with a 400ms moving average so organ swells feel like the room opening, not a zoom. Vocal channel: brightens the central rosette (radial gradient stop 0 luminance from 0.5 to 1.0, spring-damped) and increases the Cinzel glow blur-radius from 18 px to 28 px — the words feel sung into existence. Motes: eight points drifting on independent Perlin-noise paths, speed 0.3–0
proposals.productionMethod: Real-time Canvas 2D renderer. Pre-render step on load: compute and cache the 12-vector registration array, draw tracery mesh to offscreen canvas (one draw call, reused every frame). Per-frame draw order: (1) fill background #0A0B14; (2) blit offscreen tracery at 0.55 opacity; (3) draw caustic ellipses for all 12 petals with current Harmonic scale; (4) draw god-ray conic gradients at current opacity; (5) draw motes; (6) apply text-safe dimming band rect with destination-out composite to suppress scene layers within the lyric zone; (7) draw central rosette with Vocal-driven luminance; (8) draw anamorphic flare if Vocal > 0.6; (9) CSS filter pass (saturate/contrast) on canvas element; (10) lyric engine renders Cinzel line with shadowBlur glow, then word-by-word opacity reveals. Audio analysis: Web Audio API AnalyserNode, three band-pass filters (Harmonic 200–2000 Hz, Swell 20–200 Hz, Vocal
proposals.humanTrace: The lead-line registration array is the human decision that cannot be undone by a parameter slider: twelve vectors, each with its petal width and cusp radius, declared as named constants before the first render call. Every caustic ellipse, every glow boundary, every god-ray angle answers to those prior declarations — the same way a press operator commits the registration marks before the first sheet runs. The 35° god-ray azimuth is a second prior commitment, declared once, governing every specular surface in the frame. These two decisions — the 12-vector tracery and the 35° light source — are the human marks in the machine. The grain and the vignette are the material evidence that a choice was made about what kind of light this is.
proposals.risk: The risk is that this reads as too sparse for a congregation expecting luminous stained-glass grandeur — twelve lead-line vectors and eight motes against #0A0B14 could feel like a diagram rather than a window. The risk is worth it because the alternative — particle storms, layered glow on glow, every channel driving every element — produces the screensaver the brief explicitly forbids. Stillness and reverence require restraint. The registration-plate logic means the scene has structural bones that hold across the full 72-card collection: this window's geometry is a prior physical commitment, not a mood.

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist will want more — more caustic layers, more overlapping glows, more Swell drama in the radial expansion, more colour mixing in the god rays. They will argue that a Gothic rose window is inherently maximalist and that restraint here is a misreading of the architecture. I say: the window is maximalist; the renderer should not be. proposals.title: Caustic Field as Coordinate System
proposals.idea: The rose window is not a picture but a rule engine: every caustic mote, every leaded-line shadow, every bokeh bloom occupies a position licensed by the window's own radial coordinate grammar — twelve-fold symmetry, quatrefoil cusps, and a single declared light source at 35°/22° — so the scene has no decorative freedom, only derivable outputs.
proposals.geometry: Polar coordinate grid anchored at canvas center: twelve primary sectors at 30° intervals, each subdivided by the quatrefoil cusp geometry into inner medallion radius (r = 0.18vmin), petal mid-band (r = 0.18–0.52vmin), and lancet tip zone (r = 0.52–0.72vmin). Leaded tracery lines are computed strokes — not drawn assets — at cusp intersections derived from the 12-fold symmetry. A secondary Cartesian grid of 24×14 luminance-sample points governs caustic-mote placement: each mote's screen position is the polar-to-Cartesian transform of its sector index and radial band, so no mote can appear outside a geometry-licensed coordinate. Three explicit depth planes: (1) stone tracery — near, hard-edged, desaturated near #0A0B14; (2) glass petal field — mid, full chroma; (3) caustic throw and god rays — far, diffuse, additive blend. The lyric band occupies a fourth plane: a fixed horizontal strip at
proposals.typography: Cinzel, uppercase, tracked at +0.18em, set at fluid scale clamp(28px, 4.2vw, 64px) — large enough to read from 40m at 1080p. One lyric line visible at a time; word-by-word reveal on a 5-frame opacity ramp (not position shift — words do not move, they materialise). Active word: full white #FFFFFF, weight 400. Preceding words: 72% opacity, same weight. Line transitions: outgoing line fades to 0 over 18 frames; incoming line fades in over 24 frames — overlap window of 6 frames for continuity. Scripture attribution or doxology tag: Outfit Regular, 13px, 38% opacity, 2.4em below the lyric baseline, uppercase, tracked +0.22em. No drop shadow on type — the dimming band does the work. The band itself is a linear gradient from rgba(10,11,20,0) at top to rgba(10,11,20,0.72) at bottom, 160px tall, always present, never audio-reactive.
proposals.imageLogic: No concept plate. The scene is entirely procedural. The rose window geometry is constructed in Canvas 2D as a cached offscreen canvas on init: twelve sector paths clipped by inner circle and outer lancet arcs, filled with chroma values sampled from the four palette hues (#1E3A7A cobalt, #A8243B ruby, #E8A838 gold, plus computed emerald #1A6B3A not in palette but derivable as the complementary axis between cobalt and gold — flagged for team review). The leaded tracery overlay is a second cached offscreen canvas of computed stroke paths at 1.5px logical width, colour #0A0B14 at 90% opacity. At runtime, the two cached canvases are composited onto the main canvas with globalCompositeOperation 'source-over'. Caustic motes are drawn as radial gradients (not particles) at the 24×14 grid coordinates, radius 8–22px, additive blend, alpha driven by audio amplitude envelope. God rays are eight line
proposals.texture: Simulated leaded glass is achieved through two optical passes baked into the kit's Council pass: (1) a film grain layer at 0.8% noise amplitude, monochrome, blended at multiply 18% — this is the human trace of the glass medium without faking a photograph; (2) a colour fringe pass that shifts the red channel +1px and blue channel -1px horizontally at the petal boundary edges only, simulating chromatic aberration through thick antique glass. The material weave for this card is 'refractive' — the optical pass emphasises the colour-punch and anamorphic flare nodes, not the grain node, because glass transmits rather than absorbs. Bokeh bloom behind the tracery plane uses large-radius (40–90px) radial gradients at opacity 0.06–0.14, colours sampled from adjacent petal hues, positions fixed to the 24×14 grid — no random placement.
proposals.motion: Steady state is the primary specification. The rose window geometry is static — it does not breathe, pulse, or rotate. Motion is a property of the light field only, not the architecture. Three motion channels, all spring-damped with stiffness 0.06, damping 0.78: (1) Harmonic amplitude → caustic mote alpha, cycling through ruby→cobalt→emerald→gold petal sectors in sequence at 0.25Hz base rate, so colour blending is a temporal rotation not a spatial smear — each sector brightens in turn, giving the impression of light moving through the window without moving the window. (2) Swell amplitude → god ray opacity (0.04→0.12 range) and a radial scale on the bokeh bloom layer (1.0→1.08, never exceeding 8% expansion) — the aperture appears to breathe. (3) Vocal amplitude → leaded tracery rim highlight: a 2px inner stroke on the central rosette path shifts from rgba(232,168,56,0.1) to rgba(232,168,5
proposals.productionMethod: Canvas 2D renderer, two cached offscreen canvases (geometry + tracery) computed once on init and redrawn only on resize. Main render loop: clear → composite background gradient (#0A0B14 to #0D1428 radial) → blit god ray layer (redrawn each frame, 8 gradient strokes) → blit cached geometry canvas → draw caustic motes as radial gradients at grid coordinates (24×14 = 336 draw calls, acceptable on integrated GPU) → blit cached tracery canvas → draw bokeh bloom layer (12 large radial gradients, one per sector) → apply Council optical pass (grain, colour fringe, flare as canvas filter chain) → composite lyric band gradient → render type. Total draw calls per frame: ~380 plus text. Profiled target: 60fps at 1920×1080 on Intel Iris Xe. Resize handler recomputes all coordinate transforms and rebuilds both cached canvases; no hardcoded pixel values.
proposals.humanTrace: The 35°/22° light axiom is declared as a shader uniform equivalent (a JS constant) on line 1 of the renderer. Every downstream parameter — god ray angle, caustic falloff origin, colour fringe direction, bokeh bloom offset — is a trigonometric derivation of that constant. The human trace is the act of declaring that axiom: someone stood at a specific azimuth and elevation relative to a specific window and chose to make that observation the generative rule. The chromatic aberration fringe (+1px red, -1px blue) is the perceptible sign that light passed through something thick and refractive — it is not decorative, it is a consequence of the declared medium.
proposals.risk: The risk is that the scene reads as too architectural and not enough sacred — that congregants see a diagram of a rose window rather than a window. The counter-argument is that the geometry's correctness IS its reverence: a window that follows its own structural logic has more dignity than one that glows softly and means nothing. The deeper risk is the caustic mote grid at 336 draw calls per frame on low-end integrated GPUs — mitigated by caching and a LOD flag that halves the grid to 12×7 on devices reporting less than 4GB VRAM.

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist will want the tracery to animate — to draw itself on every lyric change, to make each verse a reveal. I reject this. The tracery is the architecture; it was there before the service began and it will be there after. Animating it makes it a prop. The window is the constant; the light through it is the variable. If the Baroque Dramatist wants drama, the drama is in the caustic

proposals.title: Light Through Dated Glass
proposals.idea: A procedurally traced Gothic rose window — twelve petals, quatrefoil cusps, leaded stone armature — built from declared geometry in Canvas 2D, so that every caustic falls only where the glass grants permission and every audio response is a property of the architecture, not a mood applied over it.
proposals.geometry: Polar coordinate scaffold: one declared centre point at 52% width × 46% height (slightly above true centre, as a nave rose sits above the sightline). Twelve primary petals at 30° intervals, each a bezier lancet with a pointed Gothic apex at r=0.38 viewport-height and a quatrefoil medallion at r=0.18 whose four lobes are themselves small polar bezier curves. Between petals: twelve minor tracery spandrels. Lead lines (simulated as 3–4px dark-stroke paths with a 1px warm-grey inner highlight) divide every region. Three concentric depth rings define the leaded armature: inner rosette r=0.08, medallion ring r=0.22, petal ring r=0.38. A stone oculus border ring at r=0.44 is rendered as a radially gradient filled annulus — cool grey on the outer edge bleeding to the scene dark. The full rose sits inside a square lancet arch whose springing points are at 28% and 72% of frame width; the arch itse
proposals.typography: Lyric band: Noto Serif, 52px at 1080p (scales to 104px at 4K), sentence case, tracking +0.04em, line-height 1.35. One line at a time. Word-by-word reveal: each incoming word fades in at 180ms opacity ease-out; the already-revealed words hold at full opacity; the line as a whole fades out at 320ms after the last word settles. Band position: a text-safe dimming band occupies the lower 22% of frame — a radial gradient from rgba(10,11,20,0.78) at bottom to fully transparent at the band's top edge, always rendered above every scene layer including caustics and grain. The lyric sits vertically centred in that band. Scripture reference (when present): Cinzel, 13px, all-caps, tracking +0.18em, 60% opacity, one line below the lyric, same band. No decorative rule between lyric and reference — the lead line motif from the window geometry is not borrowed for typography because that would flatten a s
proposals.imageLogic: No concept plate. The scene is entirely procedural Canvas 2D. The rose window is drawn fresh each frame from its declared polar geometry. Glass pane fills: each of the twelve petals and their sub-medallions is filled with a radial gradient whose inner colour is drawn from the palette (ruby #A8243B, cobalt #1E3A7A, emerald mixed at runtime as #1A5C3A, gold #E8A838) assigned at scene initialisation by a seeded deterministic rotation so the colour map is stable across the service. The glass fill is not flat: each pane carries a subtle inner vignette (darker at the lead edges, brighter at the pane centre) simulating glass depth and antique inconsistency — achieved by compositing a small radial gradient in 'lighter' blend mode at the pane centroid. Caustic projection: a second Canvas layer (composited in 'screen' mode) renders caustic throw shapes — elongated elliptical lozenges and trefoil h
proposals.texture: The optical pass is applied as a composited Canvas overlay at the end of each frame. Film grain: a pre-generated 512×512 noise texture (seeded, stored as an ImageData buffer at scene load) is tiled and composited in 'overlay' at 9% opacity — the grain is static per frame and re-seeded every 4 seconds with a 2-second cross-fade so it reads as slow analogue drift, not digital noise. Anamorphic flare: one horizontal streak, origin at the declared 35° azimuth entry point on the upper-left stone arch, rendered as a gradient-filled rectangle in 'screen' at 4% opacity, elongated 7:1 horizontal aspect; its opacity pulses ±1.5% with the Harmonic envelope (spring-damped, k=18, d=0.82). 35mm light leak: a warm amber radial bloom at upper-left composited in 'screen' at 6% base opacity. proposals.motion: All motion is envelope-smoothed (exponential moving average α=0.08 for slow parameters, α=0.18 for fast). Nothing strobes. Depth planes move at different parallax rates — the deep stone arch drifts ±0.4% of frame width on a 22-second sinusoidal breath; the rose window itself drifts ±0.15% on a 34-second breath; the caustic layer drifts ±0.6% on a 17-second breath. These are independent clocks, not harmonics of each other, so the scene never locks into a repeating loop. proposals.productionMethod: Canvas 2D renderer written in the Plajah kit's animation loop. Scene initialisation: declare all geometric constants (centre, petal angles, radii, lead line paths, caustic lozenge positions at 35° azimuth) as a named schema object. Pre-render the grain texture to an offscreen canvas at load. Pre-compute the twelve petal bezier path objects and cache them as Path2D instances — no path recalculation per frame. Per-frame draw order: (1) background gradient fill #0A0B14; (2) stone arch silhouette in dim gradient; (3) god ray wedges in screen; (4) caustic lozenges in screen, luminance driven by audio; (5) rose window — deep plane (stone tracery annulus), then petal fills with inner gradient, then lead lines with misregistration highlight; (6) central rosette with Vocal-driven fill; (7) mote layer in screen; (8) optical pass — grain tile, anamorphic flare, light leak, colour punch; (9) text-sa
proposals.humanTrace: The misregistration offset on the lead lines — 1px at 218° from the declared 35° azimuth — is the perceptible sign of making. It is not decorative. It encodes the physical reality that leaded glass has thickness and that light arriving at 35° will shadow the near edge of each lead line and illuminate the far edge. This offset is declared once as a constant derived from the azimuth, propagated to every lead line in the rose, and never adjusted per-line for visual comfort. The window looks built, not drawn, because one sourced physical decision was held without exception.
proposals.risk: The risk is that a procedurally traced Gothic rose, rendered without a photographed plate and without WebGL, reads as a diagram — too clean, too legible as code — rather than as a window that has held light for five hundred years. The counterweight is the misregistration, the grain drift, the antique inner-vignette on each pane, and the anamorphic flare that enters from a declared stone arch opening rather than from nowhere. If those material arguments are held as strictly as the geometry, the window earns its age. The risk is worth taking because a photographed plate would flatten the provenance — it would be someone else's window, unattributed, borrowed. A window built from its own declared geometry is the only one this scene has permission to use.

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist will want to expand the caustic throw to fill the full frame — gold flooding the nave, ruby bleeding into the text band, grandeur at maximum radius. I will not allow it. The caustics are permitted only where the geometry grants them: the ray-cast from each pane at 35° determines where the light falls on the floor plane, and that position is not negotiable for drama. proposals.title: Light That Bleeds Through Stone
proposals.idea: A procedurally-rendered Gothic rose window whose jewel caustics are not decorations but the primary dramatic actors — breathing, swelling, and casting the lyric into the congregation as though the word itself were made of light filtered through eight centuries of colored glass.
proposals.geometry: The rose window is centered at 52% horizontal, 46% vertical — slightly above true center, as a rose window sits above the nave floor, never at eye level. Twelve petals are computed as bezier arcs radiating from a central rosette of radius 0.08vw; each petal terminates in a pointed lancet at radius 0.42vw; quatrefoil cusps are inscribed at 0.28vw as four overlapping circles per petal gap, 48 total. Leaded tracery is simulated as 2–3px dark strokes (#0A0B14 at 85% opacity) separating every glass cell. Behind the window: a deep nave void — a radial gradient from #0A0B14 at center to near-black at edges, 1.8 gamma. In front of the window: three depth planes. Plane 1 (far): slow-drifting god-ray columns from the window aperture, rendered as additive radial gradient fans, 8–12 rays, 0.04–0.08 opacity, angle-jittered ±15°. Plane 2 (mid): caustic throw — the colored light that the window casts o
proposals.typography: Cinzel, all-caps, tracked at 0.22em, size 4.2vw at 1080p (scales to 3.8vw at 4K to respect reading distance). A single lyric line is always active; word-by-word reveal at 4–5 seconds per full line, each word fading in over 280ms with a very slight upward drift of 3px on entry — not a bounce, a breath. Active word: #FFFFFF at full opacity with a 0px text-shadow at 0 opacity (clean). Revealed-but-past words: #E8A838 at 72% opacity — gold, the color of the window's amber glass, so past words do not vanish but become the gilded inscription behind the living word. Incoming words are at 0% opacity until their cue. Line transitions: outgoing line fades to 0% over 600ms, new line fades in on the same beat. Text measure: maximum 72% of frame width, centered. Below the lyric: a hairline rule, 1px, #1E3A7A at 60% opacity, 280px wide, centered — this is the proscenium threshold. The text-safe dimmin
proposals.imageLogic: There is no photograph. The concept plate is the rendered scene. The window is procedurally drawn each frame to the canvas: (1) nave void gradient, (2) god-ray fan layer, (3) caustic throw blobs, (4) window geometry with leaded tracery and glass-cell fill, (5) central rosette with flare bloom, (6) bokeh mote layer, (7) dimming band, (8) lyric plane, (9) Council optical pass. The glass-cell fill is the image logic: each of the 12 petals and their sub-cells is filled with a radial gradient that simulates the internal luminosity of antique glass — not a flat color but a gradient from a brighter interior (the glass catches light at its thickest) to a slightly cooler, more saturated rim. Ruby cells: center #E8A838-tinted #A8243B, rim pure #A8243B. Cobalt cells: center #4A7FD4, rim #1E3A7A. Emerald cells: center #2D8A5E, rim #1A5C3A. Gold cells: center #F0C050, rim #E8A838. The leaded lines ar
proposals.texture: The Council optical pass carries the material weave keyed to the Baroque lens. Film grain: Perlin-noise grain layer at 0.045 opacity, scale 1.2px, reseeded every 3 frames — not animated grain but slowly evolving grain, the way emulsion shifts in a held frame. Anamorphic flare: two horizontal streak lines emanating from the central rosette, length 38–55% of frame width, #E8A838 at 0.18 opacity, width 1.5px, with a soft gaussian blur of 4px — these are the lens artifacts of photographing a rose window with a fast prime, simulated as canvas gradient strokes. 35mm light leaks: two corner vignette gradients, top-left and bottom-right, #A8243B at 0.06 opacity and #1E3A7A at 0.07 opacity respectively, rendered as radial gradients from the corners — they are not visible as light leaks, they are felt as warmth and depth. Colour punch: the entire scene passes through a soft S-curve applied via a g
proposals.motion: Everything moves slowly, everything moves at once, nothing calls attention to itself — this is the paradox of baroque stillness. The window itself: the entire rose rotates at 0.004°/s — one full revolution in 25 hours. This is not perceptible as rotation; it is perceptible as the feeling that the window is alive. God rays: each ray's opacity oscillates on a unique sine wave, period 8–14 seconds, amplitude 0.02–0.05 — they breathe. Caustic throw blobs: each blob drifts on a slow Lissajous path, amplitude 12–20px, period 18–30 seconds per axis — they wander as light on a wall wanders when a cloud passes. Bokeh motes: upward drift at 0.3–0.6 px/s, occasional very slow horizontal drift ±0.1 px/s, no respawn flicker — when a mote reaches the top 5% of frame it fades out over 2 seconds, a new one fades in at the bottom. Central rosette bloom: a radial gradient glow behind the central medallion
proposals.productionMethod: Canvas 2D, 60fps, single animation loop. Frame order: (1) clear to #0A0B14; (2) draw nave void as a radial gradient; (3) draw god-ray fan as 10 additive radial gradient wedges; (4) draw caustic throw as 36 soft elliptical radial gradients in save/restore with globalAlpha; (5) draw window: for each of 12 petals, clip to bezier arc path, fill with cell gradient, stroke tracery; draw 48 quatrefoil cusps as four-circle intersection paths, clip and fill; stroke all leaded lines; (6) draw central rosette as stacked radial gradients with bloom; (7) draw bokeh motes as small radial gradients with additive compositing; (8) draw dimming band as elliptical gradient with per-frame opacity computation; (9) draw lyric: measure text, position, apply word-state opacities; (10) apply optical pass: grain layer (Perlin noise, pre-cached 512×512 texture resampled), anamorphic streaks, corner light leaks, co
proposals.humanTrace: The leaded tracery line widths are not uniform: each segment is hand-varied between 1.8px and 3.2px using a seeded noise function keyed to segment index — this simulates the physical irregularity of lead came, which is thicker at junctions and thinner in runs. The glass-cell gradients have a slight eccentricity (center offset by 8–14% of cell radius in a direction keyed to petal angle) — this simulates the way antique glass has its brightest point where the blower's pipe was, not at the geometric center. These two decisions — uneven lead and eccentric glass light — are the maker's hand: they are not visible as decisions, they are visible as authenticity.
proposals.risk: The risk is that the window's slow rotation and the caustic drift, combined with the optical pass, produce a scene so complete in itself that it competes with the lyric rather than serving it — that the congregation watches the light move and forgets to read the word. This risk is worth taking because the alternative — a static window with a text band over it — is precisely the screensaver the brief forbids. The dimming band's dynamic deepening at high harmonic amplitude is the insurance: when the scene is most active, the word's ground darkens most, and the lyric rises. The drama serves the text or it is not drama — it is decoration.

proposals.title: One Window, One Silence
proposals.idea: Strip the rose to its governing geometry — twelve radii, one centre, stone and light — and let the caustics be the only event that breathes.
proposals.geometry: A single procedural rose rendered as pure radial structure: twelve equidistant spokes from a centred origin, each carrying one lancet silhouette (dark leaded stone, #0A0B14, 6px stroke weight scaled to viewport). Quatrefoil cusps are drawn as four tangent circles at each petal tip — no fill, outline only, so the stone reads as absence carving the coloured light. The window sits at exact viewport centre; its outer circumference is 72% of the shorter viewport dimension — large enough to dominate without bleeding to edge. One depth plane only behind the window: a radial gradient ground (#0A0B14 to #1E3A7A at 18% opacity) that holds the space without competing. God rays are suppressed at rest; they exist only as amplitude-authorized absences — the canvas darkens radially except where the audio permits light through. The lyric band occupies the lower 18% of the viewport, a dedicated horizonta
proposals.typography: Cinzel, regular weight, sentence case — not all-caps, because all-caps reads as announcement and this is confession. Size: 3.2vw at 1080p, scaling linearly to 4K. Tracking: 0.12em — wide enough to breathe, not wide enough to drift. Measure: maximum 52 characters per line; the brief's sample lines sit well inside this. Word-by-word reveal: each word fades in at 180ms opacity ease-out, previous words hold at full opacity — no movement, no slide, only light arriving. Line hold: 4.2 seconds from first word to fade. Line fade: 400ms opacity dissolve on the whole line before the next begins. The text-safe band is a 160px-tall strip, #0A0B14 at 72% opacity, feathered 32px at the top edge — not a box, a darkening of the ground. Cinzel's serifs carry enough cathedral register that no decorative frame is needed; the letterform is the ornament. Scripture attribution line (if present): Outfit Regula
proposals.imageLogic: No concept plate. The scene is entirely procedural. The rose is drawn each frame in Canvas 2D: stone tracery as closed Path2D strokes, petal fills as radial gradients keyed to the four palette colours (#A8243B ruby, #1E3A7A cobalt, #0A0B14 shadowed stone, #E8A838 gold), each petal's fill opacity driven by the harmonic amplitude channel smoothed over 120ms. Caustics are not particles — they are lensed ellipses: for each of the twelve petals, two to three elliptical highlight shapes are pre-positioned at geometrically derived coordinates (intersection of spoke and cusp tangent), drawn with globalCompositeOperation 'lighter' at low base opacity (0.04–0.08) rising to 0.18 on harmonic peaks. This produces the caustic cast-light effect using only filled ellipses and blend modes — no particle loop, no per-frame random walk. The ground receives the caustic throw as a second pass: the same ellips
proposals.texture: Film grain: a single pre-generated 512×512 noise texture (seeded, not animated) composited at 3% opacity over the full canvas — enough to read as age on a projector, invisible on a bright LED wall. This is the only texture layer. The leaded stone strokes carry no bevel, no shadow, no emboss — their weight alone (6px at 1080p) reads as physical mass. The glass petal fills use a two-stop radial gradient per petal: brighter at the cusp tip, fading toward the centre — simulating transmitted rather than reflected light. No vignette beyond the radial ground gradient. The Council optical pass contributes one 35mm light-leak: a single warm horizontal band (#E8A838, 6px tall, 4% opacity, blurred 40px) crossing the upper third of the rose at a fixed position — not animated, not audio-reactive. It reads as a moment of afternoon sun caught in the glass, not a UI event.
proposals.motion: At rest, nothing moves except the grain composite cycling through three pre-generated offsets at 2 fps — barely perceptible, enough to prevent freeze. On Harmonic amplitude: each petal's fill opacity scales from 0.55 (silence) to 0.82 (peak), smoothed with a 120ms exponential moving average. No petal moves position or scale. On Swell: the outer circumference of the rose scales from 72% to 78% of the shorter viewport dimension — a single uniform radial expansion, spring-damped (tension 0.04, friction 0.88) so it arrives slowly and returns slowly. This is the only geometric motion in the scene. On Vocal amplitude: the leaded stone stroke opacity rises from 0.85 to 1.0 and the central rosette (a single small circle at origin, 3% of rose diameter) brightens from #1E3A7A to #E8A838 over 200ms ease-in-out. The lyric band's text opacity is never audio-driven — it runs on its own editorial clock
proposals.productionMethod: Canvas 2D, 60fps, integrated-GPU safe. Init phase: compute and cache all twelve spoke endpoints, cusp circle centres, caustic ellipse coordinates, and petal gradient objects — zero per-frame geometry calculation. Render loop: clear canvas, draw radial ground gradient (one fillRect + one radial gradient), draw twelve petal fills (twelve fillRect-equivalent Path2D fills with cached gradients, opacity from amplitude scalar), draw caustic ellipses (36 ellipses maximum, composite 'lighter'), draw stone tracery (twelve stroke calls, cached Path2D), draw grain overlay (one drawImage from cached offscreen canvas, cycling three offsets), draw light-leak (one fillRect, blurred once at init and cached), draw lyric band dimming strip (one fillRect), draw lyric text (fillText per visible word). Total draw calls per frame: under 80. Grain offscreen canvas generated once at startup from seeded Math.ran
proposals.humanTrace: The twelve-spoke geometry is not approximated — it is derived from the actual proportional logic of Gothic rose window construction: the outer circle divided by a regular twelve-gon, cusp circles constructed as tangent inscribed circles at each petal tip using the standard geometric method. A human made that calculation and hard-coded the ratios. The editorial choice of which three caustic ellipse positions per petal carry the light is a directed compositional decision, not a random scatter — each position corresponds to where transmitted light through a faceted jewel lens would actually pool on a stone floor. The grain texture is seeded to a specific value chosen after visual review of three candidates. The light-leak position (upper third, not centre, not lower) was placed to avoid the lyric band and to echo the angle of afternoon sun entering a north-facing rose — a directorial choice
proposals.risk: The risk is that a congregation expecting stained-glass spectacle receives instead a geometry lesson. One window, barely moving, almost no particles, no sweeping rays — some worship leaders will call it unfinished. The risk is worth it because the alternative — a particle storm of jewel bokeh and volumetric god rays — turns the sanctuary into a screensaver and the lyric into a caption. The rose window in a real cathedral does not perform; it simply is, and the light does the work. This direction holds that position: the geometry earns its stillness, the caustics are the breath, and the words arrive into genuine quiet rather than visual noise.

I hold that every layer added past the stone-and-light binary is a layer competing with the lyric. disputes.concession: The eccentrically offset glass-cell gradient — centre displaced by 8–14% of cell radius toward the blower's pipe — is a physically sourced, structurally committed human trace, and I would carry that decision into my own proposal without alteration.

disputes.objection: The Minimalist strips the lead lines to 6px uniform strokes and calls it mass — but a Gothic window's physical authority comes from irregularity, from the places where the came thickens at a junction and thins mid-run, from the evidence that a human bent metal around glass. Six clean pixels is a diagram of a window, not a window. And suppressing god rays until audio 'permits' them is not restraint, it is withholding — the light through glass is not earned by the music, it is the prior condition the music enters. disputes.concession: The decision to hold the lyric on its own editorial clock, completely separate from audio amplitude, is correct — the text is not a mood visualizer and should not pulse to the mix.

disputes.objection: The 0.004°/s rotation of the window is the tell: it is spectacle dressed as behaviour, a perceptual trick with no rule behind it — no input changes it, no system state authorises it, it simply runs because rotation feels alive, which is precisely the screensaver logic I object to. The Lissajous drift on the caustic blobs compounds this: Lissajous is a borrowed mathematical surface applied for its visual elegance, not derived from any property of the declared light source or the window geometry, so the motion layer is decorative physics rather than consequent physics. When every element is given its own independent drift path and oscillation period, the system has no architecture — it has atm
disputes.concession: The eccentric glass-cell gradient — offset toward where the glassblower's pipe was, keyed to petal angle — is the one decision in the proposal that is genuinely derived: it encodes a physical cause into a coordinate, which is exactly the kind of prior commitment I respect.

disputes.objection: The decision to suppress god rays 'at rest' and let the canvas simply darken radially except where audio permits is not restraint — it is a refusal to stage the room. A rose window that withholds its light until sound authorises it has inverted the dramatic contract: the window is the event, the music is the witness, not the other way around. Six-pixel stone strokes and a 3% grain pass do not constitute a material world — they constitute a sketch that has decided to call its own incompleteness a philosophy.
disputes.concession: The observation that Cinzel's serifs already carry enough cathedral register to stand without a decorative frame is exactly right, and I will carry that into my own proposal without hesitation.

disputes.objection: The 3px upward word drift on entry, the gilded past-words, the two anamorphic streaks, the Lissajous caustic blobs, the seeded lead-width variation, the corner light leaks, the 0.004°/s rotation — each one is defensible in isolation, but together they constitute a budget of sensation that has no editor inside it; the proposal cannot name what it would remove, which means nothing in it was ever truly chosen. A rose window already contains twelve petals, forty-eight quatrefoil cusps, god rays, caustics, grain, and a lyric band — that is the maximum load before the eye has nowhere to rest, and the Baroque lens adds to every layer simultaneously.
disputes.concession: The eccentricity offset on the glass-cell gradient — center displaced toward the blower's pipe axis — is a single physically-sourced decision that earns its complexity, because it changes what the glass is, not merely how it looks.

synthesis.ariaSummary:
The council spent most of its time on one fault line: whether this rose window should *perform* its grandeur or simply *be* structurally present and let the light do the work. The Baroque Dramatist argued that a Gothic rose is inherently maximalist — every surface a sermon — and that restraint here is a misreading of the architecture. The Classical Mind held that in a Gothic nave the light is already there when you enter; your eye discovers it. The window does not announce itself. I took the Classical side, and here is why: the brief says 'gorgeous, slow, never a screensaver,' and the Baroque proposal's accumulation — rotation, Lissajous drift, two flare streaks, gilded past-words, corner light leaks — has no internal editor. When I asked which element the Dramatist would remove, the proposal had no answer. That is the screensaver test.

From the Baroque proposal I kept one thing the whole room agreed on, including the Minimalist: the eccentrically offset glass-cell gradient, where each pane's brightest point is displaced toward the glassblower's pipe axis rather than sitting at the geometric centre. Every director conceded this in their own disagreement notes. It is the one decision in that proposal that names a physical cause, and it is now in the direction.

The Radical Minimalist served as editor. They cut the window's slow rotation (the architecture is the constant — it cannot also be the motion), the Lissajous caustic paths (no derivation from the declared light source), the second anamorphic streak, and the gold past-word treatment. What remains is: φ-grid geometry declared before the render loop, a fixed window with caustics that breathe on the Harmonic channel, a parchment-grain material weave that scrolls at breath speed, and a lyric band on its own editorial clock that the audio can deepen but never move.

One decision is yours: the emerald fourth colour. The palette gives you three hues; a 12-petal rose needs four to avoid chromatic monotony. The team has a computed answer ready — but whether you authorise a fifth constant or redistribute the three you own is a call only you can make.

The proposal cannot name what it would remove, which means nothing in it was ever truly chosen.
